fieldValues.title: The renderer forces a caption before every fence
fieldValues.summary: A record whose content begins with a fenced block renders as a broken code block, because the renderer emits an inline Content label immediately before the field value. Every lifted example therefore opens with a one-sentence caption. That is editorially better anyway, but it is a renderer constraint dictating record content, not an authoring choice. Filed as srs-rust#973.
evidence: The renderer emits the Content label inline, on the same line, before the content field value
A content value starting with a fence produces a fence opened mid-line and not recognised
All 68 example records carry a caption sentence before the block
fieldValues.body: A rendering-layer quirk that constrains what a record may contain is a layer violation in the direction the charter cares about: presentation reaching back into semantics. The captions stand on their own merit, so the unit proceeded, but the constraint should not stay load-bearing. srs-rust#973.
